description:
v1.0 | 129 gates | 3 ticks
https://github.com/byggmesterPRO/pareto-circuits

Keeps a 32-bit number until the next write.

A register holds a number so a machine can remember it. Use it to keep a value such as a speed setting, the last key pressed, or a score that must survive until the next change.

Set the data inputs to the number you want and hold them steady until after the write. The outputs always show the stored number. The write input must be on for exactly one tick, so put a button or switch through a one-tick pulse maker first. A second tick would flip the stored number back. The memory starts at zero.

Inputs (yellow gates, first row, lowest bit first): data = x 0-31, write = x 32 (a pulse of exactly one tick).
Outputs (green gates): the stored number = x 0-31.

Profile: small, the build with the fewest gates for this size.
How it works: Each bit is an XOR gate wired to itself; a pulse flips the bits that must change.
Ticks from an input to the outputs: 0. From a pulse to the outputs: 3. Inputs steady before a pulse: 2.
Checked with thousands of random operations in a simulator. Gates include the input gates; ticks count the input gate too.

Other sizes, the generator and the full explanation:
https://github.com/byggmesterPRO/pareto-circuits/tree/main/circuits/register
